purpose: Logbook keeps the state of a piece of work, a thread, true across sessions, compactions and /clear, in the project's own git repository. It calls no model, so its own spend is none.

objectives.text: Tools answer without refusal or crash.
The document is kept true with little friction.
A thread's state is carried across sessions, compactions and /clear.

tool.call.description: One call of a logbook tool that concerns a thread, recorded after its reply is built. A call that concerns no thread is not recorded.
tool.call.writer: The logbook MCP server's tool wrapper, for every call of every tool.
questions: Which tools are called most, and how often does each refuse or crash?
Which argument fields are refused most often?
How long do tool calls take to answer?

tool.description: The name of the logbook tool that was called.
tool.measured_from: The name the tool is registered under in the logbook MCP server.
tool.includes: Every logbook tool call that concerns a thread.
tool.excludes: Calls that concern no thread, and tools of other servers.
tool.reading: Group by it to compare tools; a tool absent from the rows had no recorded call in the runs read.
tool.question: Which tools are called, and how often each?

outcome.description: How the call ended: ok when the tool replied with its result, refused when an argument or the thread's state was refused, crashed when the tool failed unexpectedly.
outcome.measured_from: The reply the tool wrapper built: a successful reply, a refusal from argument parsing or from the tool itself, or the unexpected-failure reply.
outcome.includes: Refusals of arguments and refusals the tool makes after reading the thread.
outcome.excludes: Failures of the metrics store, which never change the outcome.
outcome.reading: The share of refused and crashed among all calls describes how often a tool did not do what was asked; zero refused and zero crashed means every recorded call answered with its result.
outcome.question: How often do tools refuse or crash?

refusal_field.description: The argument or input the refusal named as wrong.
refusal_field.measured_from: The field of the refusal the tool returned, the same text its reply shows after "field: ".
refusal_field.includes: Refusals from argument parsing and from the tool itself.
refusal_field.reading: Null when the call was not refused; group refused calls by it to see which fields are refused most.
refusal_field.question: Which fields do tool calls get wrong?

call_seconds.description: The time from the call's start to its reply.
call_seconds.measured_from: The difference between the server clock read when the call arrived and when its reply was built.
call_seconds.includes: Argument parsing, the tool's own work and any git commands it ran.
call_seconds.excludes: Transport time between Claude Code and the server, and the metrics write itself.
call_seconds.reading: Higher means the call took longer to answer; zero means it answered within the clock's resolution.
call_seconds.question: How long do tool calls take?

doc.edit.description: One checked edit of a thread's working copy, recorded by the PostToolUse hook after it reconciles the working copy with the stored document. An edit that leaves the document unchanged is not recorded.
doc.edit.writer: The logbook PostToolUse hook, for every Edit, Write, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit of a thread's working copy.
questions: How often is an edit of the state document committed, refused by the checker or failed?
Which checks refuse edits most often?
How many violations does a refused edit carry?

outcome.description: How the edit ended: accepted when it was committed, refused when logbook's checks found violations, failed when reconciling the working copy returned a refusal.
outcome.measured_from: The result of reconciling the edited working copy with the thread's stored document.
outcome.includes: Every edit of a working copy that changed the document.
outcome.excludes: Edits that left the document equal to the stored one, and edits of files that are not a working copy.
outcome.reading: The share of refused and failed among all edits describes how often an edit did not reach the document; zero refused and zero failed means every recorded edit was committed.
outcome.question: How often does an edit of the state document reach a commit?

rules.description: The distinct names of the checks whose violations refused the edit, sorted.
rules.measured_from: The rule each violation carries, the name of the check in logbook's document checker that produced it.
rules.includes: Every check that produced at least one violation of the edit.
rules.excludes: How many times each check fired, which violations counts in total.
rules.reading: An empty list when the edit was not refused; unnest it to count refused edits by check.
rules.question: Which checks refuse edits?

items.description: The name of one check that produced a violation.
items.measured_from: The rule of a violation the checker returned.
items.reading: One of the checker's rule names, such as box or removal.
items.question: Which check refused the edit?

violations.description: The number of violations the checker returned for the edit.
violations.measured_from: The count of violations in the refused reconcile result.
violations.excludes: Refusals that are not violations, which failed edits carry instead.
violations.reading: Zero when the edit was not refused; higher means the refused edit broke more rules.
violations.question: How far from passing are refused edits?

refusal_field.description: The field the refusal named when reconciling the edit failed.
refusal_field.measured_from: The field of the refusal reconciling the working copy returned.
refusal_field.reading: Null when the edit did not fail; group failed edits by it to see what made them fail.
refusal_field.question: Why do edits fail before they are checked?

doc.commit.description: One committed version of a thread's state document, with the items it changed against the previous version.
doc.commit.writer: The logbook commit of a new version, whether from the working copy or from a tool.
questions: How many versions of the document are committed, and through which path?
How many criteria are ticked, struck or reopened per commit?
How often are decisions, risks and settled items added or removed?

via.description: What made the new version: edit when it came from the working copy, otherwise the name of the logbook tool that made it.
via.measured_from: The path the version took to its commit: the working copy reconcile, or the tool whose change was applied.
via.includes: Every committed version of a state document.
via.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
via.reading: Group by it to compare edits of the working copy with tool calls.
via.question: Which path keeps the document true?

criteria_added.description: The number of criteria added, ids starting c that the new version has and the previous lacks.
criteria_added.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
criteria_added.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
criteria_added.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
criteria_added.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
criteria_added.question: How many criteria added does each commit make?

criteria_ticked.description: The number of criteria ticked, whose box became [x].
criteria_ticked.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
criteria_ticked.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
criteria_ticked.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
criteria_ticked.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
criteria_ticked.question: How many criteria ticked does each commit make?

criteria_struck.description: The number of criteria struck, whose box became [~].
criteria_struck.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
criteria_struck.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
criteria_struck.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
criteria_struck.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
criteria_struck.question: How many criteria struck does each commit make?

criteria_reopened.description: The number of criteria reopened, whose box went from [x] or [~] to [ ].
criteria_reopened.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
criteria_reopened.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
criteria_reopened.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
criteria_reopened.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
criteria_reopened.question: How many criteria reopened does each commit make?

decisions_added.description: The number of decisions added, ids starting D that the new version has and the previous lacks.
decisions_added.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
decisions_added.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
decisions_added.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
decisions_added.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
decisions_added.question: How many decisions added does each commit make?

decisions_removed.description: The number of decisions removed, ids starting D that the previous version has and the new lacks.
decisions_removed.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
decisions_removed.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
decisions_removed.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
decisions_removed.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
decisions_removed.question: How many decisions removed does each commit make?

risks_added.description: The number of risks added, ids starting R that the new version has and the previous lacks.
risks_added.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
risks_added.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
risks_added.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
risks_added.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
risks_added.question: How many risks added does each commit make?

risks_removed.description: The number of risks removed, ids starting R that the previous version has and the new lacks.
risks_removed.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
risks_removed.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
risks_removed.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
risks_removed.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
risks_removed.question: How many risks removed does each commit make?

settled_added.description: The number of settled items added, ids starting S that the new version has and the previous lacks.
settled_added.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
settled_added.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
settled_added.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
settled_added.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
settled_added.question: How many settled items added does each commit make?

settled_removed.description: The number of settled items removed, ids starting S that the previous version has and the new lacks.
settled_removed.measured_from: A comparison of the items of the previous and the new version of the document, each parsed by logbook's document parser.
settled_removed.includes: Each item counted once by its id.
settled_removed.excludes: Changes to an item's wording, and repeats of an id after its first occurrence.
settled_removed.reading: Zero means none in this commit; higher means more in one commit.
settled_removed.question: How many settled items removed does each commit make?

thread.pickup.description: One pickup of a held thread by the SessionStart hook after a resume, a compaction or a /clear, recorded when the hook adds the thread's state to the session's context. A startup, or a session that holds no thread, records nothing.
thread.pickup.writer: The logbook SessionStart hook, for every resume, compact or clear start of a session that holds a thread.
questions: How often is a thread picked up after a resume, a compaction or a /clear?
How often does the whole state document fit in the added context?
How much context does logbook add at a pickup?

source.description: What started the session that picked the thread up: resume, compact or clear.
source.measured_from: The source of the SessionStart event Claude Code gave the hook.
source.includes: Every pickup of a held thread.
source.excludes: Startups, which add the list of threads and pick none up.
source.reading: Group by it to compare boundaries; a source absent from the rows had no recorded pickup in the runs read.
source.question: Across which boundaries is a thread's state carried?

delivered.description: What form of the state document the added context held: document when it held the whole document, short when only the short form with the path to read fitted.
delivered.measured_from: The branch the hook took when fitting the document, the activity lines and the running tools under its context ceiling.
delivered.includes: Every pickup of a held thread.
delivered.excludes: The activity and running-tool lines, which activity_lines and the context length describe.
delivered.reading: Short means the session had to read the working copy itself to see the whole document; document means the whole document arrived in the context.
delivered.question: Does the whole state document reach the session at a pickup?

activity_lines.description: The number of activity lines, tool calls made since the document's last update, kept in the added context.
activity_lines.measured_from: The count of activity lines the hook kept after fitting the context under its ceiling.
activity_lines.includes: Activity lines kept in the context.
activity_lines.excludes: Activity lines left out to fit the ceiling, and the running-tool lines.
activity_lines.reading: Zero means no activity line was kept, either because there was none or because none fitted; higher means more of the recent work was carried over.
activity_lines.question: How much recent work is carried into the session at a pickup?

context_chars.description: The length in characters of the context the hook added to the session.
context_chars.measured_from: The length of the additionalContext the SessionStart hook returned.
context_chars.includes: The opening line, the document or its short form, and any activity and running-tool lines.
context_chars.excludes: The one-line message shown to the user, which is not added to the model's context.
context_chars.reading: Higher means logbook placed more text in the session's context; it stands in for model spend, which logbook has none of.
context_chars.question: How much context does logbook add at a pickup?

thread.handover.description: One hand-over of a held thread by the SessionEnd hook when a session ends with /clear, so the session that starts next can pick the thread up. It carries the ending session in the envelope and has no fields of its own.
thread.handover.writer: The logbook SessionEnd hook, for every end with reason clear of a session that holds a thread.
questions: How often is a thread handed on through /clear?
Is every hand-over followed by a pickup in the next session?

doc.request.description: One request logbook made to the session to update a held thread's state document.
doc.request.writer: The logbook PostToolUse hook after a milestone tool call, and the logbook Stop hook after a turn that changed something or after the user wrote while the thread is blocked or waiting.
questions: How often does logbook ask for the document to be updated, and why?
Which kind of request is most frequent?

reason.description: Why logbook asked: milestone after a milestone tool call such as a commit, push or pull request, turn-changed after a turn that changed something, blocked-user-wrote after the user wrote while the thread was blocked or waiting.
reason.measured_from: The kind of the update reason the hook passed to logbook's update request.
reason.includes: Every update request a hook returned to the session.
reason.excludes: Hooks that made no request, including a repeat milestone in the same prompt.
reason.reading: Group by it to compare the kinds of request; a reason absent from the rows had no recorded request in the runs read.
reason.question: What makes logbook ask for the document to be updated?

summary.description: One line per thread run holding the thread's figures.

status.description: The thread's status when the summary was written.
status.measured_from: The kind of the Status line of the thread's current state document, read by logbook's document parser.
status.includes: The six kinds a Status line can carry.
status.excludes: The reason a blocked, waiting or abandoned status gives, and any earlier status.
status.reading: Done means the thread closed with its criteria met, abandoned that it closed without; parked, active, blocked and waiting mean it is still open. Null means the document could not be read or its Status line has no known kind.
status.question: How did the thread end, or where does it stand?

lifetime_seconds.description: The time from the run's first event to this summary.
lifetime_seconds.measured_from: The difference between the ts of the first line of the run's event file and the summary's own ts.
lifetime_seconds.includes: Time the thread spent parked as well as held.
lifetime_seconds.excludes: Time before the run's first recorded event.
lifetime_seconds.reading: Higher means the thread lived longer; zero means the run's event file held no line or the summary was written at the first event's instant.
lifetime_seconds.question: How long does a thread stay open?

sessions.description: The number of distinct sessions that wrote an event to the run.
sessions.measured_from: The count of distinct non-null session values over the run's event file.
sessions.includes: Every session id an event line carries.
sessions.excludes: Lines with a null session, written by a process given no session id.
sessions.reading: One means a single session did all the recorded work; higher means the thread was carried across more sessions.
sessions.question: Across how many sessions is a thread carried?

tool_calls.description: The number of logbook tool calls recorded for the thread.
tool_calls.measured_from: The number of tool.call lines in the run's event file.
tool_calls.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
tool_calls.excludes: Calls that concern no thread, which are not recorded.
tool_calls.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
tool_calls.question: How many tool calls does a thread take?

tool_refusals.description: The number of tool calls that were refused.
tool_refusals.measured_from: The number of tool.call lines in the run's event file whose outcome is refused.
tool_refusals.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
tool_refusals.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
tool_refusals.question: How often are a thread's tool calls refused?

tool_crashes.description: The number of tool calls that failed unexpectedly.
tool_crashes.measured_from: The number of tool.call lines in the run's event file whose outcome is crashed.
tool_crashes.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
tool_crashes.excludes: Calls that answered or were refused.
tool_crashes.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
tool_crashes.question: How often do a thread's tool calls crash?

refusals.description: The refused tool calls grouped by tool and refused field, ordered by tool then field.
refusals.measured_from: The tool.call lines of the run whose outcome is refused, counted by their tool and refusal_field.
refusals.includes: One record per pair of tool and field that was refused at least once.
refusals.reading: An empty list means no call was refused; unnest it to count refusals by tool and field.
refusals.question: Which tools and fields are refused for this thread?

items.description: One tool and field with the number of times calls of that tool were refused naming that field.
items.measured_from: A group of the run's refused tool.call lines.
items.includes: One pair of tool and field.
items.reading: Each record is one pair; count is at least one.
items.question: Which field of which tool was refused, and how often?

tool.description: The name of the refused tool.
tool.measured_from: The tool of the refused tool.call lines.
tool.question: Which tool was refused?

field.description: The argument or input the refusals named as wrong.
field.measured_from: The refusal_field of the refused tool.call lines.
field.reading: The same text the refused reply shows after "field: ".
field.question: Which field was refused?

count.description: The number of refused calls of that tool naming that field.
count.measured_from: The count of the run's refused tool.call lines with that tool and refusal_field.
count.reading: At least one; higher means the same refusal recurred.
count.question: How often was that field of that tool refused?

edits_accepted.description: The number of working-copy edits that were committed.
edits_accepted.measured_from: The number of doc.edit lines in the run's event file whose outcome is accepted.
edits_accepted.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
edits_accepted.excludes: Refused and failed edits, and edits that left the document unchanged.
edits_accepted.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
edits_accepted.question: How many edits of the working copy reach a commit?

edits_refused.description: The number of working-copy edits logbook's checks refused.
edits_refused.measured_from: The number of doc.edit lines in the run's event file whose outcome is refused.
edits_refused.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
edits_refused.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
edits_refused.question: How often are edits of the working copy refused?

edits_failed.description: The number of working-copy edits whose reconcile returned a refusal before any check.
edits_failed.measured_from: The number of doc.edit lines in the run's event file whose outcome is failed.
edits_failed.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
edits_failed.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
edits_failed.question: How often do edits of the working copy fail?

edit_rules.description: The checks that refused edits, each with the number of refused edits it refused, ordered by check.
edit_rules.measured_from: The rules of the run's doc.edit lines whose outcome is refused, each rule counted once per edit.
edit_rules.includes: One record per check that refused at least one edit.
edit_rules.reading: An empty list means no edit was refused; unnest it to count refused edits by check.
edit_rules.question: Which checks refuse this thread's edits?

items.description: One check with the number of refused edits it refused.
items.measured_from: A group of the run's refused doc.edit lines by rule.
items.reading: Each record is one check; count is at least one.
items.question: Which check refused edits, and how often?

rule.measured_from: A rule of a refused doc.edit line.
rule.reading: One of the checker's rule names, such as box or removal.
rule.question: Which check refused the edit?

count.description: The number of refused edits the check refused.
count.measured_from: The count of the run's refused doc.edit lines whose rules hold that check.
count.excludes: How many violations of the check an edit carried.
count.reading: At least one; higher means the check refused more edits.
count.question: How often did that check refuse an edit?

commits.description: The number of versions of the state document committed.
commits.measured_from: The number of doc.commit lines in the run's event file.
commits.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
commits.excludes: Refused and failed edits and tool calls, which commit nothing.
commits.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
commits.question: How many versions of the document does a thread take?

criteria_added.description: The number of criteria added over the thread's commits.
criteria_added.measured_from: The sum of criteria_added over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
criteria_added.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
criteria_added.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
criteria_added.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
criteria_added.question: How many criteria added does a thread make?

criteria_ticked.description: The number of criteria ticked over the thread's commits.
criteria_ticked.measured_from: The sum of criteria_ticked over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
criteria_ticked.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
criteria_ticked.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
criteria_ticked.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
criteria_ticked.question: How many criteria ticked does a thread make?

criteria_struck.description: The number of criteria struck over the thread's commits.
criteria_struck.measured_from: The sum of criteria_struck over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
criteria_struck.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
criteria_struck.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
criteria_struck.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
criteria_struck.question: How many criteria struck does a thread make?

criteria_reopened.description: The number of criteria reopened over the thread's commits.
criteria_reopened.measured_from: The sum of criteria_reopened over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
criteria_reopened.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
criteria_reopened.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
criteria_reopened.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
criteria_reopened.question: How many criteria reopened does a thread make?

decisions_added.description: The number of decisions added over the thread's commits.
decisions_added.measured_from: The sum of decisions_added over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
decisions_added.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
decisions_added.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
decisions_added.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
decisions_added.question: How many decisions added does a thread make?

decisions_removed.description: The number of decisions removed over the thread's commits.
decisions_removed.measured_from: The sum of decisions_removed over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
decisions_removed.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
decisions_removed.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
decisions_removed.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
decisions_removed.question: How many decisions removed does a thread make?

risks_added.description: The number of risks added over the thread's commits.
risks_added.measured_from: The sum of risks_added over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
risks_added.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
risks_added.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
risks_added.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
risks_added.question: How many risks added does a thread make?

risks_removed.description: The number of risks removed over the thread's commits.
risks_removed.measured_from: The sum of risks_removed over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
risks_removed.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
risks_removed.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
risks_removed.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
risks_removed.question: How many risks removed does a thread make?

settled_added.description: The number of settled items added over the thread's commits.
settled_added.measured_from: The sum of settled_added over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
settled_added.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
settled_added.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
settled_added.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
settled_added.question: How many settled items added does a thread make?

settled_removed.description: The number of settled items removed over the thread's commits.
settled_removed.measured_from: The sum of settled_removed over the doc.commit lines of the run's event file.
settled_removed.includes: Every commit of the run, whether from the working copy or a tool.
settled_removed.excludes: Versions that were refused or failed, which are never committed.
settled_removed.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
settled_removed.question: How many settled items removed does a thread make?

criteria_total.description: The number of criteria in the thread's current state document.
criteria_total.measured_from: The count of items with an id starting c in the current document, read by logbook's document parser.
criteria_total.reading: Zero means the document lists no criterion.
criteria_total.question: How many criteria does the thread carry?

criteria_open.description: The number of criteria in the current state document whose box is empty.
criteria_open.measured_from: The count of items with an id starting c and an empty box in the current document, read by logbook's document parser.
criteria_open.reading: Zero means every criterion is ticked or struck; higher means more work is left.
criteria_open.question: How much of the thread's work is still open?

pickups_resume.description: The number of pickups of the thread after a resume.
pickups_resume.measured_from: The number of thread.pickup lines in the run's event file whose source is resume.
pickups_resume.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
pickups_resume.excludes: Pickups from other sources, and startups.
pickups_resume.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
pickups_resume.question: How often is the thread picked up after a resume?

pickups_compact.description: The number of pickups of the thread after a compact.
pickups_compact.measured_from: The number of thread.pickup lines in the run's event file whose source is compact.
pickups_compact.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
pickups_compact.excludes: Pickups from other sources, and startups.
pickups_compact.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
pickups_compact.question: How often is the thread picked up after a compact?

pickups_clear.description: The number of pickups of the thread after a clear.
pickups_clear.measured_from: The number of thread.pickup lines in the run's event file whose source is clear.
pickups_clear.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
pickups_clear.excludes: Pickups from other sources, and startups.
pickups_clear.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
pickups_clear.question: How often is the thread picked up after a clear?

pickups_short.description: The number of pickups that delivered only the short form of the document.
pickups_short.measured_from: The number of thread.pickup lines in the run's event file whose delivered is short.
pickups_short.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
pickups_short.excludes: Pickups that delivered the whole document.
pickups_short.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
pickups_short.question: How often does the whole document not fit at a pickup?

handovers.description: The number of times the thread was handed on through /clear.
handovers.measured_from: The number of thread.handover lines in the run's event file.
handovers.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
handovers.excludes: Session ends with any reason other than clear.
handovers.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
handovers.question: How often is the thread handed on through /clear?

requests_milestone.description: The number of requests to update the document with reason milestone.
requests_milestone.measured_from: The number of doc.request lines in the run's event file whose reason is milestone.
requests_milestone.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
requests_milestone.excludes: Requests with other reasons, and hooks that made no request.
requests_milestone.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
requests_milestone.question: How often does logbook ask for an update with reason milestone?

requests_turn_changed.description: The number of requests to update the document with reason turn-changed.
requests_turn_changed.measured_from: The number of doc.request lines in the run's event file whose reason is turn-changed.
requests_turn_changed.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
requests_turn_changed.excludes: Requests with other reasons, and hooks that made no request.
requests_turn_changed.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
requests_turn_changed.question: How often does logbook ask for an update with reason turn-changed?

requests_blocked_user_wrote.description: The number of requests to update the document with reason blocked-user-wrote.
requests_blocked_user_wrote.measured_from: The number of doc.request lines in the run's event file whose reason is blocked-user-wrote.
requests_blocked_user_wrote.includes: Every matching line the run's event file holds when the summary is written.
requests_blocked_user_wrote.excludes: Requests with other reasons, and hooks that made no request.
requests_blocked_user_wrote.reading: Zero means none in this run; higher means more.
requests_blocked_user_wrote.question: How often does logbook ask for an update with reason blocked-user-wrote?

context_chars.description: The total length in characters of the context logbook added at the thread's pickups.
context_chars.measured_from: The sum of context_chars over the thread.pickup lines of the run's event file.
context_chars.excludes: The one-line messages shown to the user, and the context added by startups and update requests.
context_chars.reading: Zero means no pickup was recorded; higher means logbook placed more text in sessions' context; it stands in for model spend, which logbook has none of.
context_chars.question: How much context does logbook add over a thread's life?
